plain: Able to be formally charged with a serious crime.

webster.text: That may be indicted; as an indictable offender.

more.text: Subject to be presented by a grand jury; subject to indictment; as an indictable offense.

example.quote: He wished to know in what court the members of the government were to be tried for the commission of indictable offences, or injuries to individuals.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 14, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
